primary_source.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder

secondary_claim_checked: A machine-generated summary characterized the profile construction as conditional on Assumption 12.1, allegedly not discharged by the paper.

primary_source_crosswalk.assumption: Section 12.1 lists the joint compatibility requirements for the assembly theorem and says Theorem 12.4 proves them for the concrete construction.
primary_source_crosswalk.existence_statement: Theorem 12.4 states that compatible construction data exist.
parameter_order: Fix admissible dimensionless outer data P_* and delta and the axis shift j.
Choose the core scale Lambda after those data are fixed.
Increase C_* subject to finitely many stated lower bounds, with R_ref=110(C_* P_*)^10, rebuilding dependent profiles and moments.
Close the five-moment tolerance and verify all four clauses of Assumption 12.1 for the same data.
primary_source_crosswalk.common_quantities: Theorem 12.4 states that the waiting length tau and restored axis pressure P0pre are fixed across the sufficiently-large-C_* family.

finding: The secondary summary is incomplete if it implies the compatibility requirement remains an unresolved existence assumption. The primary source explicitly states and proves a simultaneous-choice theorem; its warning is against varying one parameter while freezing dependent data.
limits: Textual/source-level cross-check only; Theorem 12.4 and the cited supporting lemmas were not independently proved here.
The lower-order coefficient induction was not audited.
Part II residual cancellation remains unlocated and unverified.
No conclusion about the complete OpenAI construction, a solver defect, or physical behavior follows.
